Published by TroubleMaker Media Group / Midgard Media LLC Cover art and design by TroubleMaker Media Edited and Formatted in the United States of America Chapter One: Still Of The Night Ferdinand crouched low in the field; dusk had slowly settled over the land shrouding everything in the waning light of the evening sun. Shadows began to stretch as if reaching out and trying to touch the living. He could hear the shallow raspy tone of his own breath and it felt as if his heart was going to explode out of his chest. Ferdinand took a few deep calming breaths, trying to settle his heart and calm his shaking hands. He scanned the twilight looking for anything out of place, or any movement from the tree line. As he studied the shadows of the bushes and trees, he said a prayer and crossed himself, his armor no longer filled him with the confidence of a second skin as he moved it made small scraping sounds as the joints rubbed together. He winced as it did it again. He knew his quarry had the hearing of a forest predator and would be able to pick out that sound as if it were a beacon alerting them to his location. He quietly began to take off the Armor, he removed his gloves and laid them on the ground quietly, every time the armor made a sound he would pause to ensure it had not garnered the attention of anything nearby. Ferdinand quickly removed his pauldrons and then his gorget. Exposing his neck and the leather straps for the chest piece. Once he had completed removing his armor, he crouched there with only linen pants and a shirt feeling the cool breeze as it dried his sweat that covered his body and face. His eyes continued to scan the tree line, he knew it was out there, had heard it, that blood curdling sound that commenced the hunt. He never looked down as he felt around and then found his sword and scabbard. The Red Cross on the pommel standing out against the white pearl and gold hilt. He took a good grip on the sword and slowly slid it out of the scabbard. He winced as the sword, in contact with the metal ring at the top of the scabbard began to make a scraping noise, he quickly lifted it a little so it wouldn’t contact the ring. In a moment the sword was free and in his hand. He felt infinitely better with the weapon ready to use. The bishop who had sent him here had told him this was a group not a single creature and that they hunted as a pack, isolating a victim and once they were away from lights and people, they would pounce. Ferdinand had read the accounts and seen the sketches of what had been left. They were demons, monsters they had attached and mutilated children and women. This was the work of the devil himself. He said another prayer to Michael to strengthen his resolve. Ferdinand was scared, trembling even; this was not his first hunt; there had been many since he first swore his secret oath all those years ago. He had continued to faithfully serve the church since becoming Emperor. As the years passed he knew this day would come; and it filled his heart with dread; it had been 10 years since his last hunt. As Emperor he had become complacent in his training, Ferdinand was painfully aware that he was not as nimble as he once was. But he was here, once again hunting demons in the dark, fulfilling his Oath; after all being Emperor did not excuse him from his duty; as the Bishop delighted in reminding him. He had explained that the Pope had sent three hunters after this group and none had returned, He was the last and he carried Lobera, his sword, it was special, but only in his hands so the church had been forced to call upon its greatest hunter, the one they called the Invincible Warrior of Jesus Christ. No one except his most trusted body guard knew and that was only because he had to recruit his friend and guard to assist him in getting out of the castle, Ferdinand fanned himself with his free hand the night was unseasonably warm for Austria in April it was going to be a hot summer he thought. A sound to his left startled him and Ferdinand swung his sword towards it letting out a hiss. The sword made contact loudly with a metal gauntlet and then was lowered by the man who had come upon him “My lord, we see no sign of this thing you speak of, surely it is not here” Said Ulbricht, captain of his guards. Ferdinand shook his head “My friend it has an incredible ability to hide, even for one so large, but mark me it is here and when you least expect it, it will be upon you and with haste. Keep your wits dear friend, I would hate to lose you this night” Ferdinand whispered to his friend and body guard. “Where are the other men” He asked scanning the tree line again. “They are dispersed along the south line, they were told to be quiet and report anything out of the ordinary.” Ferdinand nodded to himself “What did you tell them” he asked arching an eyebrow at his friend. Ulbricht looked at him a bit sheepishly “I told them a wild boar was loosed in these parts and we were to assist the Emperor in hunting it” He shrugged and looked back towards where the men were spread out “I am not sure they believed it, but they will be vigilant and when the time comes they will strike should you need it sire” Ferdinand nodded “thank you old friend, I know the story is unbelievable, but I have seen these creatures and hunted them before, I do not wish the nightmares I am about to incite upon you, but I needed your help, I am no longer able to take these creatures alone” Ferdinand felt shame when he said it out loud, that is why he was scared. He was older and slower and had not trained in many years. This time he was afraid he would not walk away from this. “We are here Sire, we will ensure your protection even at the cost of our own lives, should this beast make itself known” Ulbricht stated Ferdinand could see in his eyes, he did not believe his Emperor about the creature. Oh my friend you will soon enough and then you too will not be able to sleep more than a few hours, for that I apologize, I did not wish to pass my burden onto anyone else. A tortured scream floated over the field from the tree line and Ferdinand broke out in fresh sweat as he listened. Ulbricht tilted his head to focus on where the sound was coming from. “It’s Percival” he exclaimed and took off for the tree line. Ferdinand was right behind him, keeping a death grip on his sword and continuing to scan the tree line. The scream lasted for only about 20 seconds and then abruptly cut off. Only the echo of it floated over the field for a moment, and then the only sound that could be heard was the rushing of feet as he and Ulbricht make their way to the source of the noise. A light out of the corner of Ferdinand’s eye caught his attention, The sword, it had begun to glow in the night air, light at first and then as they approached the glow became brighter. “Ulbricht slow your pace; we are among enemies” he said with a hushed voice. They slowed their pace and now that the scream had stopped it was eerily quiet. The mist had settled upon the fields this night heavier than they usually would have this time of year. As they neared the forest they could hear a dragging sound somewhere in front of them, it stopped as soon as they got within 20 paces of the forest edge. Ferdinand put a hand against his friend’s chest. “This is my fight, I will need you to stay here In case something happens my friend” Ulbricht was about to protest but he knew the look in the emperors eyes when something was a command and not a suggestion. He bowed his head slightly and stood his ground, as Ferdinand slowly paced forward the sword at the ready. The ground crunched beneath his feet having not rained in many days. His face was slick with sweat. He was afraid, afraid of not being fast or strong enough, it had been too long. And he knew it, the beast could probably smell the fear rippling off his body. His foot touched upon something slick he pointed the glowing sword down to see the white and red of bloody entrails as they snaked off into the woods. Oh yes the best had been here and had done its evil work. He slowly followed the pieces of bone and meat into the forest. Walking as silently as he could and scanning the forest in front of him. The beast would fear the sword, this he knows, one touch would burn its flesh as one strike would sear through its evil bone and muscle like butter. The creature as all its kind could sense the weapon and the power it commands. This was one of the power of the hunters, those who commanded holy weapons against such creatures, as he had done for all these years. He heard the crack of a twig to his left and as he turned something large flung through the woods to his right. He heard a guttural chuckle but could not ascertain where it had come from. This was not right, these creatures feared these weapons and those who wielded them, this beast should be running causing Ferdinand to hunt it down. But it stayed, it toyed with him. “Did you not think that time would catch up to you old man.” The guttural voice said from everywhere at once. Ferdinand stopped cold, this creature could talk, this was not like the ones he had hunted before. He only knew of one creature of this ilk who had the ability to keep its full human wits, a prince, one of the original six touched by Satan himself. But no one had laid eyes on such a creature in centuries. The sweat dried from his body as fear fully took hold of him. This was not a normal hunt, nor a normal creature. “Show yourself demon, for I know what you are” he said into the night with as much gusto as he could muster. And that eerie cold rough chuckle came from the woods again, mocking him with its inability to be sourced. “You will die creature as those of your ilk have before at my hands” Ferdinand said into the forest as he slowly circled, looking for any signs of the creature. Another branch snapped and behind him he could feel claws rake across his back as something large passed him. He swung his sword, missing whatever it had been by mere inches. The pain on his back was excruciating but helped to better clear his mind. “Sire do you require assistance” Ulbricht yelled, Ferdinand could hear the voices of the other men around him probably having come from their own positions upon hearing his yelling. “NO, stay where you are” he said with all the authority he could muster. “That’s right old man, this is your fight, as it has been for many years, they would just get in the way” The creatures guttural tongue taunted him. Suddenly he remembered, why was he playing to this beast, the sword was not the only weapon he possessed. He closed his eyes and said an Aramaic incantation, when he opened them, they glowed and he could see as if it were daylight, and three in the distance outlined in red was the creature. It was the biggest one he had ever seen. Lord it was huge. It moved with a speed that Ferdinand could barely see as his eyes tracked it, He closed them again and began to say another incantation that would give him the strength he needed to defeat the best. But that had been his undoing, before he could finish, He felt a searing pain in his had and opened his eyes to see that is arm was gone, as was the sword. Ferdinand opened his mouth to scream when a large set of teeth descended and clamped around his shoulder. It dragged him off quickly as he screamed and screamed. Ulbricht could take no more, he ordered his men into the forest. They spread out and searched for their king. All they found was the arm and the sword. By daybreak they had all but given up. Ulbricht ordered them to keep searching, he wrapped the arm and sword in his own tunic and rode back for Vienna, the Bishop would want to know what happened. IT took him a full day of riding to reach the chapel where the bishop was housed. He dismounted his horse and entered the chamber where the bishop was writing in a book. Angrily he flipped open his tunic and the arm and sword rolled across the desk of the bishop. “I don’t know you name sir, or what power you have over my king, but this is all that is left. I ask that you let us form a full contingent and search for him immediately. The bishop stared at the arm thoughtfully and asked Ulbricht to recite the story exactly as he remembered it. He started at the beginning at by the end the old Bishop looked very troubled. All he said was “A prince took a king” and then shook his head. Ulbricht recited his demand for the full contingent and the old Bishop nodded his head. “No the King died peacefully in his bed in Vienna, the whole of the country will mourn and not a word of this will be spoken, do you understand me Ulbricht. He said with a forceful tone. Ulbricht protested and the Bishop produced a ring and a letter, he handed them to Ulbricht to read then, and then reread them.  “This is from the king” he said in awe  “Yes my son”, said the bishop, “giving me full authority to handle this matter the way I see fit, do you understand “ Ulbricht nodded, what would you have me do. The bishop took the sword and put it in a box, where he handed it to a lower clergy who quickly disappeared, from under his desk he produced another which looked quite like the other he had just whisked away. “You are you ride this night, carry this sword and this letter to Don Yuan Manuel, he will know what to do, other than that you are not to speak to anyone about this, do you understand. Ulbricht hung his head and nodded, he would comply with his kings last wished Chapter Two: Daily Grind The alarm went off at 5 AM as it did every day. Victor, rolled over and kissed his wife, who wouldn’t be up for another two hours, the baby still slept in the room with them and had been up for a few hours the night before. The kids also wouldn’t be starting their day for at least the same amount of time, but as with every weekday, work was calling and as every morning he thought about calling in sick, but he needed the paycheck more then he needed the time off. He took a shower and then wiped the steam from the mirror and there looking at himself was an older version of the young man he remembered, a little heavier, but not too heavy to be considered fat but the grey in his chest hair and sneaking its way into his temples and with brown hair it was easier to see the grey, he had kept himself clean shaven for at least 5 years since he had first seen the signs of grey snaking through his beard, hoping to stave off the look of age for as long as possible. But the chest grey and the laugh lines on his face gave away his 37 years of life. “A little older but still kicking my friend” he said to himself in the mirror. He had thought about dying his hair but his wife always winced at that and told him she liked the grey, it made him look distinguished, he thought she was full of shit, but didn’t have the heart to disregard her on this so he never had done it. He pulled the newly pressed Khaki Park Police uniform from the plastic that the dry cleaners seem to always put them in and put it on, smoothing out the creases, he then pulled on the tactical boots that he had shined the night before and admired the polished look of them before moving over to the closet, pulling his gun from the locker he kept in the closet a Nickel Plated.38 revolver with a 6 inch barrel and black Hogue grips, Jessica never liked him having a gun in the house, but it was part of the job, they had agreed he could as long as he kept it locked up when at home. He strapped his backup to his leg another 3-inch barrel.38, lord knows why he carried either, he had never had to shoot someone in anger and even the drunks in the park had never given him too much trouble. He had been assigned duty at the C&O Canal, Maryland Side for going on 10 years now it was a good job and he liked it, just he would have liked it more if it paid better, with two kids and living in this part of Maryland it wasn’t cheap. He left house he had barely been able to afford in the suburbs of Gaithersburg, near the lake forest mall, back when they bought the place, once he had gotten assigned here, Gaithersburg had been a nice up and coming area. Now it was a good place to live but with Germantown and Frederick the new hotspots, it was beginning to look a bit aged. He got into his 91 Toyota Celica and pulled out of the driveway it wasn’t much to look at but it was paid for and allowed him the ability to afford the car payment on Jessica’s Sienna Van, which since it was for the kids it allowed him to justify it, without getting too depressed. Long since had the days of cools sports cars passed him by, He still had his aged Harley Softail in the garage, but he rarely got time to ride it and Jessica had been on him since the birth of their first child to get rid of it, every time she heard a story or saw a news report of someone getting killed on a bike, the old argument would reignite itself. But he always stood his ground and hence had won that argument repeatedly. He always tried to get out early traffic on 270 was hell if you had too late of a start. He merged onto the highway from Middlebrook road and started his daily trip. Everything was as normal until he hit Macarthur Blvd. Traffic shouldn’t have been this heavy but the closer he got to the great falls entrance the more he realized that traffic was almost at a standstill. It took Vic an hour to reach the gatehouse, Johnny who worked the late shift was still manning the gate, turning everyone away. Vic rolled down the window, “hey man what’s going on?” he asked as he noticed all of the unmarked, marked and park police vehicles lined in the lot. Johnny was about 25 and his short cut blonde hair with the ever present sun burn when his hat as off was a good joke to most of the guys who worked with him, the curse of the Irish they would say to him good naturedly. Vic continued to stare at the vehicles in the lot “Oh man Vic, they have been asking for you for like an hour man, you need to get to the visitor hall now, isn’t your cell phone on? Which of course it wasn’t Vic usually turned it on when he got to work just to avoid the early morning bill collector calls. Vic looked confused, “Who has been asking for me” Johnny just shook his head, “the old man, and he is not happy” Shit Vic thought Captain Robert Shilling “The Old Man” as everyone called him was a hard ass who liked to run things like he was still in the marine corps, personally he hated Vic and well the feeling was mutual, if The Old Man was asking for him, it was definitely not going to be a good day. “I don’t know what happened but something big is going on.” He waived Vic in, and as he pulled past the litany of cars he noticed federal plates, State Police, Local Police quite a few Park Police vehicles and a limo, which seemed very out of place Vic pulled his old Celica in next to the limo, made sure to turn on his cell phone which immediately said he had 10 voice mails, probably all from the Captain and his Mounty cap from the passenger seat. He didn’t know what he had done but the old man was the Sr. Officer here and if he was being asked for then he was probably in trouble. Vic had a bit of an issue with authority, but he had been able to keep a lid on it mostly and had only been in trouble a hand few a times. But this sounded like something big. As he walked into the visitor center which had seemed to become a impromptu command post there was a Hodge podge of people, State police, guys in suits, park police and yes Priests. He didn’t know what they were doing here but this really wasn’t good. Seemed to be arguments over something and of course there were some snippets of conversation over who had jurisdiction over this. This was a mess, that much Vic knew and he was about to be put into the middle of it. It was going to be a very bad day. He didn’t get two steps before his name was called and everyone turned to see who had entered. Vic sighed and turned “Sir, what’s up” he walked over to the group in the corner which consisted of two priests and two guys in suits. As Vic approached he saw the familiar wide shoulders and blonde hair and realized he knew the priest, well the younger one and his mouth just about fell open. “Vic, you are being assigned to the father here” The old man said and from the look on his face he was not happy about it, the old man still wore that high and tight haircut and kept himself fit, hell you could bounce a quarter off his stomach that matched with the wide shoulders, starched uniform and boots that were practically mirrors, he was the vision of a retired Marine Officer. Vic was a little confused, he looked between the suites and the priest, He was at a loss, he had no idea what a couple of clergy were doing here, or what the hell was going on, but the day just got better and better. “Does someone want to fill me in, I am feeling a little at a loss” he said trying to get a grip on himself. The old man’s bushy eyebrows came together to form that uni-brow that everyone joked he got when angry shook his head. “As of 3:30 this morning what was left of a body washed up on the shore of the canal not 3 miles from here, it was discovered by a patrolman and called in, within two hours we had these guys”, he pointed to the suites “from the Justice department and these guys” pointing at the priests “from the Vatican, apparently the Justice Department has Jurisdiction, and the Vatican sent these guys as consultants. So now you know as much as I am allowed to. Within an hour of going through our records, they pulled your name out and said they wanted you as their liaison. So congratulations, you are now assigned to the Justice Department” Said the Captain using that booming baritone he liked to show off to anyone within ear shot. What the fuck, was all Vic thought, he looked at his old friend who was dressed complete with black suite and white collar and figured that’s why he got pulled for this duty, Sam wanted a friendly face. The younger priest held out his hand “Hey Vic” Vic smiled and took it, “Sam, I would have never thought to see a Jesuit priest at a murder scene, I am guessing you had something to do with this little assignment” Father Lawrence looked a bit sheepish “I apologize after going through the files Bishop Talbot here picked you but since we knew each other, it didn’t hurt, how are you, still attending church?” he asked innocently Vic just shook his head “Jessica takes the kids on Sunday, I try not to if I can help it, no offense, just we agree to disagree about certain topics” he said looking into his old friends eyes and seeing the sadness, I am sorry about the loss of your parents I am I know it’s been ages since we were choir boys at St Marks, but I understand your reservations.” Vic looked around at all the suits “So you want to tell me what a couple of priests are doing at this little shin dig” He could see his friends eye shift, Vic knew that look from when they were kids, it’s something he did when he wasn’t being truthful, he could never lie very well “We are here as consultants on the case, it might be ritualistic in nature” Okay Vic decided to leave it alone, so since I guess I am here to lias, what’s my duties. Bishop Talbot stepped up and introduced himself “Mr. Handy I am Sr. Bishop Talbot, I see you know my young colleague The bishop extended his hand and Vic shook it, “Sir, I am not sure what you think I can do that the Captain can’t I am sure he would be a better choice as a liaison then myself” Vic said looking towards the Captain and seeing that same stern look he always had. “No son I think you are exactly who we need” and the Bishop left it at that. “You will be our guide while here as well as interface with the Park and local police on our behalf should we need to, Smith and Park here will be our federal liaison’s with Justice” Vic nodded it almost sounded like the priests were in charge. Which would be a lot weirder then things already were, he was about to say something that would probably have earned him quite the disciplinary action until. Sam, who knew him all too well sensed what was coming saved him “Well let’s go see the site shall we”. Sam grabbed His friend by the arm and gently led him out of the building before he could speak another word. And the procession went outside into the morning sun. The park was eerily empty and aside from police cars the lot was absent of the usual runners and bikers who so frequented the park on a daily basis. The precession walked over to two Gator’s that were parked near the visitor center and the drivers Vic knew as fellow park officers, seemed quiet and a little pale in the face, His guess was this was not the first lot to visit the site and that didn’t speak well for what he was going to see. They rode along the path of the canal for about two or three miles and as they pulled up to the area Vic could see police tape setup as well as a crime lab van from Rockville as well as some State Police cars. They unpacked themselves from the Gator’s and while they waited for their escort Vic took a moment to scan the area, As he was looking towards the far side of the canal he thought he could see two people in the woods near the banks, Must be hikers doing a little rubber necking he thought and dismissed it. Bishop Talbot walked up behind Vic and laid a hand on his shoulder. “Father Lawrence tells me you served in the military young man” He looked back at the Bishop and nodded 11 Bravo infantry, I was Airborne he said and then looked away hopefully the Bishop taking the hint he didn’t want to talk about it anymore. Unfortunately, he didn’t “I hear you served overseas, see any action” Vic sighed, it was going to be one of those days. “Not a lot sir, I was at Camp Casey Korea and aside from a little small arms fire, not a lot was going on” Vic walked forward the Bishops hand slipping from his shoulder as he rushed a little both to get away from the older man and to catch up to his friend. He leaned into Sam “Couldn’t you guys have found someone else for this gig Sam, I mean you’re not doing me any favors here, the amount of paperwork alone is going to have me cursing your name for a month” Father Lawrence just shook his head, “Sorry Vic, it wasn’t my call the bishop insisted it had to be you, not sure why but I couldn’t talk him out of it, he saw your name and then he made a few calls, after that even your boss couldn’t talk him out of it” Vic found that a little odd, “Who did he call?” Sam just shook his head, not sure, but Vic saw that look again, His friend was holding something back, he would have to get him alone and find out what all this mystery was, well once they got through this. They approached the site of the body and Vic stopped in his tracks, pieces of bone and intestine were strung at least 50 feet up the shore along with an arm and from what he could tell, what was left of a leg “Jesus, what kind of monster would do this” he whispered Sam visibly flinched “Why would you say that” he asked defensively. Vic looked at him and shook his head, “Really, you think a sane man would do this to a person, hell I would have thought a bear or something just from the fact this guy looks ripped apart”. “A bear would have eaten more of the body and not left a lot of the intestine strewn, nor would it have spread the carcass so far along the short” came a baritone voice from behind Vic which damn near made him jump out of his skin. He turned to come face to face with a man who had to be a head taller than Vic himself and since Vic was 6 feet even that was saying something. The man’s full beard had a small amount of grey but his eyes were what really bothered Vic, they were a slate blue and seemed to stare right through you. He was wearing a pair of jeans and a flannel shirt and looked more like a lumberjack then a cop. “Excuse me” Vic said The man just smiled “A bear would have eaten most of this and kept it in a smaller area, this body wasn’t eaten, it was torn apart and then strewn here to be found, more like a statement then a prey kill, Edgar Johnson, I am here with his eminence as there animal expert” and Edgar held out his hand, You must be Victor Handy Vic took the hand and it was a strong grip, but not too strong “I am, but what would a couple of priests need with an animal expert” he asked realizing this was just getting weirder and weirder. Edgar scanned the remains and walked a few feet only stopping once or twice to take a glance at something. “this was a trophy kill, it was left for us to find almost like a marker, they wanted to get someone’s attention, just not sure who” he said rubbing his beard as he thought. “It was almost like it knew…” that was as far as he got before the Bishop cleared his throat and shot him a look. It didn’t escape Vic but he didn’t mention it, just filed it away. There was more to this than anyone was letting on. He would have to grill his old friend because if they threw him in the middle, he sure as shit wasn’t going to walk around blind. And why choose him anyway, this made no sense, this whole day in fact had too many questions than answers for his liking. “Do you mind if I take a quick look at the remains Sam” he asked his old friend. Same glanced at the Bishop who apparently gave his consent with a barely noticeable nod. “Go ahead, but be careful we don’t want evidence tainted”. Vic made his way under the police tape taking notice that Edgar and the Bishop were in somewhat of a heated debate. He was not liking this at all. He had never actually worked a murder so wasn’t sure what he was looking for, But he had seen dead bodies though not quite in this bad of a condition. He looked closely at what he assumed was a torso, there were tear marks made from something large, like a knife but in a pair of 4 consecutive marks. “Now that’s a bit odd” he said to himself more than anyone else. There was no way a person could have done this much damage to a body and those tear marks were too big for a bear. He was in over his head and he just wanted to know how much shit he was in. Chapter Three: In The Name Of The Father Sam was not happy, not happy at all his eminence was specific about choosing Victor, He wouldn’t tell him why. But Same knew what they were hunting and he definitely didn’t want his friend to be brought into the middle of this. The Bishop knew something that he was keeping to himself. This kill made no sense, it wasn’t like all the others this was too high profile, too easy to find dammit and that was the problem. They had gotten the call from there contact at the DOJ and within a few calls they had their Justice escorts and were on their way. He had not been with the order long, only about a year but the things he had seen would be enough to drive any sane man mad. They had hunted 2 since he had been brought into the fold. Only he, the bishop and three others of the order knew what they did and more importantly what they hunted. They currently had 6 hunters at their disposal of which Edgar was the best. They were lucky he was in Virginia tracking a pack that had come across from Ohio when this happened. He had high tailed it here within two hours and was on scene. Sam thought Edgar was as perplexed as the rest of them, not once had a body been left so blatantly for them to find. It was like they were baiting them, or someone. Sam knew they were searching for something. The family killed in San Bernardino last year, the Old man and his grandson in Ohio. But this was a nobody, a runner with no connection or family name. But the fact that it had been left here, of all places for anyone to find, they had to know hunters would be crawling all over the area within a day and that no rock would be left unturned. Why would they risk this, what would it gain them Too many questions with no answers and Sam didn’t like it. The Bishop was also stonewalling him. Making him choose his childhood friend as the liaison he didn’t even know they knew each other until he handed Sam the folder and he said something, the small smile on the face of the Bishop was odd. It was like a piece had fit together and Sam just didn’t see it. Edgar knew something was up. He could see him and his eminence talking in hushed tones but Edgar clearly was upset. He would have to find out why later, since the Bishop wouldn’t tell him maybe Edgar would. Same scanned the trees and held the silver cross he kept in his pocket tightly. They could be watching, that would be like them wouldn’t it, waiting to see who showed up, see if they could get the scent of the hunter. Sam watched Vic as he looked over the scene, he didn’t want Vic in this, not with Jessica and the kids at home. If they were watching what would happen if they marked him thinking he was a hunter. Sam would never forgive himself if anything happened to his friend or the family, after his parents had died the kids and Jessica were all he had. He had lost his way, Victor was a good catholic, like himself they loved the church, worked it every Sunday helping father Duncan with anything they could, hell they were altar boys together. But after the car accident Vic had stopped going to church, he had stopped everything It wasn’t until years later when he had heard his friend had gotten married that he had hope that he might return to a normal life. Sam said a quick prayer for his friend. “Father Lawrence, could I have a word with you, in private” called Bishop Taylor. Breaking Sam out of his thoughts. He turned to look at the bishop and could see the serious set in his face “Of course your eminence” He turned back to where Vic was examining a piece of the corpse “Vic, ill be right back, if you have any questions please ask Edgar, and again please don’t touch anything until the crime lab has a chance to go through it” Vic waved at him and Sam stepped over to the Bishop. “Walk with me father, please” the bishop said extending his hand up the canal walk, “Of course sir” he started up the dirt path with the Bishop next to him. Sam strolled along the path for a few minutes appreciating the trees but his mind a turmoil of questions and worries, once they were far enough from the others Same stood looking at the trees “Sir, I have issues with this, it makes no sense for them to leave a body like this, are we sure it was them?” Sam asked hopeful. “The bishop just stared out over the Woodline, “Edgar used the cross, it was them and they were here as recently as within an hour of the body being found so they stayed long enough to ensure that it happened.
